title: OKR Framework Measurable Performance
setup: Ten days after legacy completion (12/16/1323). Victory achieved and legacy established, but rebellion lacks performance measurement—unable to track progress or identify weaknesses. Drawing from Doerr's Measure What Matters OKRs, advisory council proposes Performance Measurement Architecture: Clear Objectives defining aspirational goals, Key Results quantifying success (2-3 per objective), Weekly Check-Ins reviewing progress. Implementation creates 81% goal clarity, measurable progress tracking, and continuous improvement within 18 days.

title: Task Maturity Adaptive Metrics
setup: Five weeks after OKR implementation (01/20/1324). Metrics creating clarity but one-size-fits-all approach struggling—different teams at different maturity levels needing different measurement approaches. Drawing from Grove's High Output Management Task-Relevant Maturity, Marcus proposes Adaptive Metrics Framework: Team Maturity Assessment evaluating competence per task, Tailored Performance Indicators selecting appropriate metrics, Dynamic Oversight Adjustment adapting support to maturity. Implementation creates 76% metrics relevance, team-appropriate measurement, and optimized performance within 22 days.

title: Intrinsic Motivation Performance Excellence
setup: Eight weeks after Adaptive Metrics (03/16/1324). Metrics optimized but compliance-oriented—teams hitting numbers without engagement or initiative. Drawing from Pink's Drive Autonomy/Mastery/Purpose, advisory council proposes Intrinsic Performance Framework: Autonomy Goal Setting offering choice in objectives, Mastery Practice Opportunities providing growth paths, Purpose-Task Linkage connecting metrics to meaning. Implementation creates complete performance architecture. Within 27 days: peak performance emerging, intrinsic motivation driving excellence, sustainable high output normalizing. Performance complete: measured, adaptive, intrinsically motivated.
